purpose: deterministic fallback when live AI is unavailable

city.summary: A city can attract people and concentrate activity, but it will also demand food, water, and energy.
immediate: Population pressure may rise around the new settlement.
Nearby routes and resource flows may become more important.
later: Homes, markets, schools, roads, and power links may develop around it.
risks: Rapid growth can strain food, water, energy, and ecology.
city.surprise: A city placed near another active object may quickly become the center of a new visible relation.

forest.summary: A forest can strengthen ecology and provide a place for resources, movement, and recovery.
immediate: Nature may improve around the forest.
People may begin moving between nearby settlements and the forest.
later: Water, gardens, rivers, or community activity may grow around it.
risks: Fire or excessive use can damage the forest edge.
forest.surprise: A nearby city may create a people-and-timber flow instead of leaving the forest isolated.

volcano.summary: A volcano can provide energy opportunities while creating a serious hazard for nearby life.
immediate: Nearby people may avoid the danger zone.
Energy potential may increase.
later: Geothermal development, evacuation routes, or new settlements may appear.
risks: Ash, fire, and displacement can reduce hope and ecology.
volcano.surprise: A dangerous volcano can become useful when connected to energy infrastructure.

energy.summary: An energy source can unlock growth and visible activity in nearby structures.
immediate: Available power may rise.
Nearby cities or workshops may become more active.
later: Industry, markets, schools, or wind infrastructure may develop.
risks: Energy production may consume water or increase ecological pressure.
energy.surprise: A power link to a city can become one of the clearest visible relationships in the world.

idea.summary: An idea can raise hope and open new development paths without needing a large physical footprint.
immediate: People may gain a new direction for development.
later: Schools, communities, workshops, gardens, or homes may emerge from it.
risks: An idea without supporting resources may remain symbolic.
idea.surprise: A small idea can redirect the next choices more strongly than a large structure.

water.summary: Water can support people, farming, ecology, and future settlement.
immediate: Water availability may improve.
Food and ecology may benefit nearby.
later: Fields, gardens, rivers, cities, or forests may develop around it.
risks: Too much concentration around one water source can create dependency.
water.surprise: Water can become the missing link that activates several nearby objects at once.

mountain.summary: Mountains can shape movement, shelter, energy, and future routes.
immediate: Travel may become more constrained or redirected.
later: Roads, bridges, wind power, homes, or rivers may become logical developments.
risks: Isolation can slow interaction between distant areas.
mountain.surprise: A mountain can become valuable when a road or bridge turns it from a barrier into a landmark.

farm.summary: Fields can increase food production but depend on water, routes, and markets.
immediate: Food reserves may improve.
Water demand may rise.
later: Irrigation, markets, roads, cities, or gardens may develop.
risks: Drought or poor transport can limit the benefit.
farm.surprise: A nearby river can transform fields into a visible irrigation chain.

road.summary: A road can connect existing objects and turn isolated places into an active network.
immediate: Movement between nearby places may become easier.
later: Markets, bridges, cities, homes, and workshops may grow along the route.
risks: Roads can increase ecological pressure and attract growth into fragile areas.
road.surprise: A simple road may change where people move even without creating a new resource.

school.summary: A school can strengthen hope, knowledge, and the ability to generate new developments.
immediate: Local hope may rise.
later: Ideas, communities, medicine, workshops, or cities may become more likely.
risks: A school without food, energy, or nearby residents may have limited effect.
school.surprise: Education can become a source of future actions rather than only a passive building.

market.summary: A market can turn nearby production into exchange and attract people and routes.
immediate: Food and activity may circulate more visibly.
later: Roads, farms, cities, workshops, and homes may develop around trade.
risks: A market without supply routes may have little to exchange.
market.surprise: A farm-market link can become the start of a real logistics chain.

rain.summary: Rain can restore water and ecology while changing fire, rivers, and fields.
immediate: Water, food, and ecology may improve.
later: Fields, rivers, forests, gardens, or water systems may strengthen.
risks: Too much water can eventually create flooding pressure.
rain.surprise: Rain near fire can create an immediate visible extinguishing relationship.

workshop.summary: A workshop can convert energy and materials into useful activity and new production.
immediate: Local production activity may increase.
later: Energy, markets, roads, cities, or new ideas may connect to it.
risks: It can consume energy faster than the world can supply it.
workshop.surprise: A workshop can turn an abstract idea into a visible production chain.

medicine.summary: Medicine can support population stability and increase hope near settlements.
immediate: People may recover or remain in the area.
later: Homes, communities, schools, gardens, or cities may grow around care.
risks: Medicine still depends on food, energy, and access.
medicine.surprise: A medical point can become a migration attractor during a nearby crisis.

wind.summary: Wind can create cleaner energy and reshape which places are useful for power.
immediate: Energy availability may improve with low direct ecological cost.
later: Energy systems, farms, roads, communities, or towers may develop.
risks: Wind alone may be unreliable without storage or other power sources.
wind.surprise: A remote windy area can become important once a road or energy link reaches it.

bridge.summary: A bridge can create a new route across water or difficult terrain.
immediate: Movement between separated areas may improve.
later: Roads, markets, cities, and homes may grow around the crossing.
risks: A bridge without useful destinations on both sides may add little value.
bridge.surprise: One bridge can reroute many people at once by shortening their paths.

night.summary: Night changes visibility, energy demand, movement, and the value of lighted places.
immediate: Energy demand may become more noticeable.
later: Homes, cities, towers, energy, or controlled fire may gain new importance.
risks: Low energy can reduce activity and hope after dark.
night.surprise: Night can reveal which parts of the world are truly connected to power.

sun.summary: Sunlight can support food and energy while increasing pressure on water.
immediate: Food and energy potential may improve.
later: Fields, gardens, power, water systems, or cities may develop.
risks: Dry conditions can reduce water availability.
sun.surprise: Sun can help one system while creating a new problem for another.

river.summary: A river can become a source of water, food, movement, ecology, and new routes.
immediate: Water and nearby food potential may improve.
later: Bridges, fields, cities, water systems, and forests may develop along it.
risks: Flooding or poor crossing points can divide areas.
river.surprise: A river beside fields can immediately create a visible irrigation relationship.

home.summary: Homes attract residents and can turn scattered activity into a neighborhood.
immediate: Population may gather more strongly around the area.
later: Cities, roads, gardens, communities, and markets may grow nearby.
risks: More residents increase demand for food, water, and energy.
home.surprise: Several small homes can gradually reshape the center of population without a large city action.

garden.summary: A garden can improve food, ecology, and hope in a small local area.
immediate: Food and nature may improve modestly.
later: Water, homes, communities, forests, or fields may connect to it.
risks: A garden can struggle without reliable water.
garden.surprise: A garden near homes can create a soft green center for a growing settlement.

tower.summary: A tower can become a landmark, observation point, or infrastructure anchor.
immediate: The area may gain visibility and identity.
later: Roads, cities, energy, wind systems, or schools may develop around it.
risks: A tower can consume resources without solving an immediate shortage.
tower.surprise: A tower in the right location can later become part of a communication or energy network.

cloud.summary: Clouds can signal future rain and change water, food, and energy conditions.
immediate: Water conditions may become more favorable.
later: Rain, water systems, forests, fields, or wind activity may follow.
risks: Reduced sunlight can temporarily reduce some energy or farm benefits.
cloud.surprise: Clouds can become the first step in a rain-to-fire or rain-to-farm chain.

fire.summary: Fire provides energy and warmth but can spread into nearby natural areas.
immediate: Energy may rise locally while water and ecology come under pressure.
later: Water, rain, community response, roads, or forest damage may follow.
risks: Nearby forests can ignite and create a visible spreading-fire relation.
fire.surprise: A dangerous fire can also generate new emergency routes and community behavior.

community.summary: A community can coordinate people and make several nearby systems work together.
immediate: Hope and local cooperation may rise.
later: Homes, schools, markets, gardens, or cities may develop around shared activity.
risks: A community still needs enough food, water, and energy to remain stable.
community.surprise: A community can connect several smaller structures into a functioning settlement.
